subproblem.statement: Conventions (as in the selected node): ℝ^P = Euclid P, ℝⁿ = Euclid n, Hᵈ = μHE[d], e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 ∈ ℝ^P, x_i the i-th coordinate. n := m + 1. For a pair p = (z, ι) ∈ ℤ^P × (Fin n → Fin P): Φ_p(y) := z + Σ_{j<n} y_j e_{ι(j)} for y ∈ ℝⁿ (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.1 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.2 j) (1 : ℝ)); e_p := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}); Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} with Lebesgue measure (volume); F_p := {x ∈ ℝ^P : z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 for i ∈ range ι, x_i = z_i for i ∉ range ι} (the closed unit face of the selected node's statement); A_p := Φ_p(Q₁) (the open face). 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d (domain univ throughout); ∂X = X.boundary; M_W(X) = X.massOn W and M(X) = X.mass (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm); IMRep and IsIntegerMultiplicity are the contract notions. Then (I) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) and p ∈ s, y ↦ w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(e_p) is integrable on Q₁; (II) there is D ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with D(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(e_p) dy for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P); (III) every D ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) satisfying this formula has M(D) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁}|w_p|).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, (29) and the mass estimate in (34) via 2.35, as used in step 6 of the parent proof ("Pc is linear and |Pc(ω)| ≤ (Σ|β_p|)·sup|ω(e_ι)|, so it is sequentially continuous on test forms"; "M(Q − Pc) ≤ Σ∫|θ_p − β_p|"), stated for general L¹ densities w_p.

1. Pointwise bounds. Let ω be a test n-form. It is continuous with compact support, so ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_x ‖ω(x)‖ < ∞ (operator norm of continuous alternating maps). For every x and p ∈ s, |ω(x)(e_p)| ≤ ‖ω(x)‖·∏_k ‖e_{ι(k)}‖ = ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ ‖ω‖_∞. Moreover, since ι is strictly increasing and basisFun i = e_i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply), ω(x)(e_p) is the term indexed by I = ι in covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} ω(x)(basisFun∘I)²)^{1/2}; hence |ω(x)(e_p)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)).

2. (I). For p ∈ s, y ↦ ω(Φ_p(y))(e_p) is continuous (Φ_p is affine, hence continuous; ω is continuous; evaluation at the fixed tuple e_p is continuous), hence AE-strongly measurable, and it is bounded by ‖ω‖_∞ (step 1). Since w_p is integrable on Q₁, the product y ↦ w_p(y)·ω(Φ_p(y))(e_p) is integrable on Q₁ (Integrable.bdd_mul / Integrable.mul_bdd).

3. (II). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) let L(ω) := Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} w_p(y) ω(Φ_p(y))(e_p) dy. Because (ω + ω')(x)(v) = ω(x)(v) + ω'(x)(v) and (cω)(x)(v) = c·ω(x)(v), (I) and linearity of the integral (integral_add, integral_smul) show that L is linear. Sequential continuity: let ω_j → 0 in the sense of TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. Then there is a compact K with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j → 0 uniformly on K; since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f(x)‖ and ω_j = 0 off K, ε_j := sup_x ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0. By step 1, |L(ω_j)| ≤ Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} |w_p(y)|·ε_j dy = ε_j·Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁}|w_p| → 0. Hence L is a continuous current in the sense of GeometricCurrentOn univ n; this is the required D.

4. (III). Let D ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) satisfy the formula and let ω be admissible for M(D) = M_{ℝ^P}(D), i.e. covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x. By step 1, |ω(Φ_p(y))(e_p)| ≤ 1 for all y and p ∈ s, so by (I) and integral_mono, D(ω) ≤ Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} |w_p(y)|·|ω(Φ_p(y))(e_p)| dy ≤ Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁}|w_p|. Hence ofReal(D(ω)) ≤ ofReal(Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁}|w_p|) for every admissible ω, and taking the supremum (sSup_le) gives M(D) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁}|w_p|). ∎
proof_key_steps: |ω(x)(e_p)| ≤ ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ ‖ω‖_∞, and |ω(x)(e_p)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) since e_p is a strictly increasing coordinate frame.
Integrable × bounded continuous is integrable on Q₁.
The formula is linear and bounded by (Σ∫|w_p|)·sup|ω|, hence sequentially continuous on test forms: it defines a current.
Admissible forms satisfy |ω(e_p)| ≤ 1, so M(D) ≤ ofReal(Σ_p ∫_{Q₁}|w_p|).

subproblem.title: Coordinate covectors dx^J: duality with the coordinate frames e_I and the Euclidean coefficient norm of their combinations (Simon Ch. 6, §1, 1.1, 1.2 and 1.5; the covectors of steps 3–4 of the parent proof)
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ. Write ℝ^P = Euclid P, e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 and, for I : Fin k → Fin P, e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(k−1)}). There is a family dx : (Fin k → Fin P) → Covector(ℝ^P, k) of continuous alternating k-linear forms on ℝ^P (the coordinate covectors dx^J = dx^{J(0)} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{J(k−1)}) such that (i) for all strictly increasing I, J : Fin k → Fin P, dx^J(e_I) = 1 if I = J and dx^J(e_I) = 0 if I ≠ J; and (ii) for every N ∈ ℕ, every injective family J : Fin N → (Fin k → Fin P) of strictly increasing maps and every c : Fin N → ℝ, covectorEuclideanNorm(Σ_{l<N} c_l·dx^{J_l}) = (Σ_{l<N} c_l²)^{1/2}. Here covectorEuclideanNorm(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin P strictly increasing} α(b_{I(0)}, …, b_{I(k−1)})²)^{1/2} with b = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (the Euclidean coefficient norm of SimonGMT).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ), ∃ dx : (Fin k → Fin P) → Covector (Euclid P) k, (∀ I J : Fin k → Fin P, StrictMono I → StrictMono J → dx J (fun r => EuclideanSpace.single (I r) (1 : ℝ)) = if I = J then 1 else 0) ∧ ∀ (N : ℕ) (J : Fin N → Fin k → Fin P) (c : Fin N → ℝ), Function.Injective J → (∀ l, StrictMono (J l)) → covectorEuclideanNorm (∑ l, c l • dx (J l)) = Real.sqrt (∑ l, c l ^ 2)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, §1 (chapter-06.txt, "Preliminaries: Vectors, Co-vectors, and Forms"): 1.1 (ω₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ ω_k(v₁, …, v_k) = Σ_σ sgn σ ω_{σ(1)}(v₁)⋯ω_{σ(k)}(v_k) = det(ω_i(v_j))), 1.2 (every k-covector is Σ_α ω_α dx^α over increasing multi-indices α, with ω_α = ω(e_α)) and 1.5 (the dx^α, α increasing, are orthonormal, so the Euclidean norm of Σ_α ω_α dx^α is (Σ_α ω_α²)^{1/2}; this is SimonGMT's covectorEuclideanNorm). The parent proof uses them in step 4 (the test forms Σ_l (−1)^l g_l dx^{ι(0)} ∧ ⋯ (dx^{ι(l)} omitted) ⋯ ∧ dx^{ι(m)}) and in step 3 (an n-covector α with α(e_ι) = 1 to read off the orientation sign). Notation: e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1, e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(k−1)}), v_j the j-th coordinate of v ∈ ℝ^P, [A] := 1 if A holds and 0 otherwise.

1. Construction. For J : Fin k → Fin P let f_J be the continuous multilinear map (ℝ^P)^k → ℝ, f_J(v) := ∏_{r<k} (v_r)_{J(r)}; in Lean f_J := (ContinuousMultilinearMap.mkPiAlgebra ℝ (Fin k) ℝ).compContinuousLinearMap (fun r => EuclideanSpace.proj (J r)). Put dx^J := ContinuousMultilinearMap.alternatization f_J, a continuous alternating map, i.e. an element of Covector (Euclid P) k (no finite-dimensionality argument is needed for continuity). By ContinuousMultilinearMap.alternatization_apply_apply, for every v : Fin k → ℝ^P,
  dx^J(v) = Σ_{σ ∈ Equiv.Perm (Fin k)} sign(σ) • ∏_{r<k} (v_{σ(r)})_{J(r)}
(sign(σ) ∈ {±1} acting on ℝ by multiplication; this is the Leibniz expansion of det[(v_c)_{J(r)}]_{r,c}). For k = 0 the only permutation is the identity and the empty product is 1, so dx^J(v) = 1.

2. Duality (i). Let I, J : Fin k → Fin P be strictly increasing and v := e_I. Since (e_i)_j = [i = j] (PiLp.single_apply; EuclideanSpace.single_apply is its deprecated alias), the σ-term ∏_r (e_{I(σ(r))})_{J(r)} equals 1 if I(σ(r)) = J(r) for every r, i.e. I ∘ σ = J, and 0 otherwise. Suppose I ∘ σ = J. As I is strictly increasing, I(a) < I(b) ⟺ a < b (StrictMono.lt_iff_lt); so for r < r', I(σ(r)) = J(r) < J(r') = I(σ(r')) gives σ(r) < σ(r'): σ is a strictly increasing map Fin k → Fin k. Its range is all of Fin k (σ is a bijection), which is also the range of id; two strictly increasing maps on Fin k with the same range coincide (StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so σ = id and hence J = I. Consequently, if I ≠ J every σ-term vanishes and dx^J(e_I) = 0; if I = J, the only nonzero term is σ = id (every σ with I ∘ σ = I is the identity, by the same argument), so dx^J(e_I) = sign(id)·1 = 1. This proves (i).

3. Values of combinations. Let N ∈ ℕ, J : Fin N → (Fin k → Fin P) injective with every J_l strictly increasing, c : Fin N → ℝ and α := Σ_{l<N} c_l·dx^{J_l}. For every strictly increasing I : Fin k → Fin P, (i) gives α(e_I) = Σ_l c_l·[I = J_l]. By injectivity of J at most one l satisfies J_l = I, so α(e_I) = c_l if I = J_l, and α(e_I) = 0 if I ∉ range J; in both cases α(e_I)² = Σ_l c_l²·[I = J_l].

4. The norm (ii). By definition covectorEuclideanNorm(α) is the square root of Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin P} (if I is strictly increasing then α(b∘I)² else 0), where b = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ satisfies b_i = e_i (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply), so α(b∘I) = α(e_I). By step 3 this sum equals Σ_I [I strictly increasing]·Σ_l c_l²[I = J_l] = Σ_l c_l²·Σ_I [I strictly increasing ∧ I = J_l] = Σ_l c_l² (exchange the two finite sums, Finset.sum_comm; for each l exactly one I, namely J_l, is counted, because J_l is strictly increasing). Hence covectorEuclideanNorm(Σ_l c_l·dx^{J_l}) = (Σ_l c_l²)^{1/2} = Real.sqrt (Σ_l c_l²). (If k > P there are no strictly increasing maps, so (i) is vacuous and (ii) only concerns N = 0, where both sides are 0.) ∎

Source: Simon Ch. 6, §5 (the cubical grid and its faces F ∈ 𝓛_n, of Hⁿ-measure 1, used throughout the proof of 5.1), as stated in step 1(a), (c), (d) of the parent proof (φ_p is an isometric embedding with φ_p([0,1]ⁿ) = F_p and φ_p((0,1)ⁿ) = F_p°; μHE[n] is preserved by isometries and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ; diam F_p ≤ √P; F_p is closed; distinct open faces avoid the other closed faces). Notation as in the statement; since ι is strictly increasing it is injective, so n ≤ P. ê_k is the k-th standard basis vector of ℝⁿ.

1. Coordinates of Φ_p. The i-th coordinate of e_{ι(j)} is 1 if i = ι(j) and 0 otherwise, and ι is injective; hence (Φ_p y)_{ι(k)} = z_{ι(k)} + y_k for every k < n and (Φ_p y)_i = z_i for every i ∉ range ι.

2. (6), and Φ_p is a measurable embedding. By step 1, Φ_p(y) − Φ_p(y') has coordinate y_k − y'_k at ι(k) and 0 at every i ∉ range ι, so ‖Φ_p(y) − Φ_p(y')‖² = Σ_k (y_k − y'_k)² = ‖y − y'‖², i.e. dist(Φ_p(y), Φ_p(y')) = dist(y, y'). Thus Φ_p is an isometry ℝⁿ → ℝ^P (Lipschitz with constant 1, continuous, injective); an isometry from a complete space has closed range and is a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), hence a measurable embedding (Topology.IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding).

3. (5) and F_p = Φ_p(C), C := [0,1]ⁿ. If 0 ≤ y_k ≤ 1 for all k, step 1 gives (Φ_p y)_{ι(k)} ∈ [z_{ι(k)}, z_{ι(k)} + 1] and (Φ_p y)_i = z_i for i ∉ range ι, so Φ_p(y) ∈ F_p: this is (5). Conversely, for x ∈ F_p put y_k := x_{ι(k)} − z_{ι(k)} ∈ [0,1]; by step 1, Φ_p(y) and x have the same coordinates, so x = Φ_p(y). Hence F_p = Φ_p(C) and, Φ_p being injective, Φ_p⁻¹(F_p) = C.

4. (1), and Q₁ = C almost everywhere. The coordinate map ℝⁿ = Euclid n → (Fin n → ℝ) is measure preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp, equivalently EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp); it maps Q₁ onto the box ∏_k (0,1) and C onto ∏_k [0,1]. By volume_pi_Ioo and volume_Icc_pi both boxes have volume ∏_k ofReal(1 − 0) = 1. So volume(Q₁) = 1 = volume(C) < ∞, and as Q₁ ⊆ C, volume(C ∖ Q₁) = 0, i.e. volume⌞C = volume⌞Q₁ (equivalently Measure.univ_pi_Ioo_ae_eq_Icc).

5. (8). F_p = ⋂_{i<P} S_i with S_i := {x : (i ∈ range ι → z_i ≤ x_i ∧ x_i ≤ z_i + 1) ∧ (i ∉ range ι → x_i = z_i)}. For fixed i exactly one of the two implications is non-vacuous, so S_i is {x : z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1} or {x : x_i = z_i}, the preimage of a closed subset of ℝ under the continuous coordinate map x ↦ x_i. So every S_i, and hence F_p, is closed; in particular F_p is Borel.

6. (3). On Euclid n, μHE[n] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Since Φ_p is an isometry, Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure gives Φ_p#(volume) = Φ_p#(μHE[n]) = μHE[n]⌞(range Φ_p). Restrict both sides to the Borel set F_p ⊆ range Φ_p (step 3). On the left, by MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map and step 3, (Φ_p#volume)⌞F_p = Φ_p#(volume⌞Φ_p⁻¹(F_p)) = Φ_p#(volume⌞C) = Φ_p#(volume⌞Q₁) (step 4). On the right, (μHE[n]⌞range Φ_p)⌞F_p = μHE[n]⌞(F_p ∩ range Φ_p) = μHE[n]⌞F_p (Measure.restrict_restrict, F_p Borel). Hence μHE[n]⌞F_p = Φ_p#(volume⌞Q₁).

7. (2). Evaluating (3) on ℝ^P: Hⁿ(F_p) = (μHE[n]⌞F_p)(ℝ^P) = (Φ_p#(volume⌞Q₁))(ℝ^P) = volume(Q₁) = 1 by (1).

8. (4). Because Φ_p is a measurable embedding, MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map gives ∫ f d(Φ_p#ν) = ∫ (f∘Φ_p) dν for every f : ℝ^P → ℝ, integrable or not. With ν := volume⌞Q₁ and (3): ∫_{F_p} f dHⁿ = ∫_{Q₁} f(Φ_p(y)) dy.

9. (7). Let x, x' ∈ F_p. For i ∉ range ι, x_i = z_i = x'_i; for i ∈ range ι, x_i, x'_i ∈ [z_i, z_i + 1], so |x_i − x'_i| ≤ 1. Hence dist(x, x')² = Σ_{i ∈ range ι} (x_i − x'_i)² ≤ #(range ι) = n ≤ P and dist(x, x') ≤ √P.

10. (9). Let q = (z', ι') with ι' strictly increasing, y ∈ Q₁ and x := Φ_p(y), and suppose x ∈ F_q. By step 1, for k < n, x_{ι(k)} = z_{ι(k)} + y_k with 0 < y_k < 1, so x_{ι(k)} ∉ ℤ. As x ∈ F_q, x_i = z'_i ∈ ℤ for every i ∉ range ι'. Hence every ι(k) lies in range ι', i.e. range ι ⊆ range ι'. Both ranges have exactly n elements (ι, ι' injective on Fin n), so range ι = range ι'; two strictly increasing maps Fin n → Fin P with the same range coincide (each is the increasing enumeration of that set: Finset.orderEmbOfFin_unique, or StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so ι' = ι. For i ∉ range ι, z'_i = x_i = z_i (x ∈ F_q and step 1). For i = ι(k), z_i < x_i < z_i + 1 and z'_i ≤ x_i ≤ z'_i + 1 with z_i, z'_i ∈ ℤ: z'_i ≥ z_i + 1 would give x_i ≥ z_i + 1, and z'_i ≤ z_i − 1 would give x_i ≤ z_i, both impossible; so z'_i = z_i. Thus z' = z and ι' = ι, i.e. q = p. Consequently, if q ≠ p then Φ_p(y) ∉ F_q. ∎

subproblem.title: A set that coincides near x with the affine plane x + V has approximate tangent space V at x (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4; used for the open faces in step 6 of the parent proof)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, N ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P), x ∈ ℝ^P, V a linear subspace of ℝ^P with dim V = n (Module.finrank ℝ V = n), and r > 0 such that for every y with |y − x| < r: y ∈ N if and only if y − x ∈ V. Then N has approximate tangent space V at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x V, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4: dim V = n and ∫_{blowUpMap x λ '' N} f dHⁿ → ∫_V f dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), where blowUpMap x λ y = λ⁻¹(y − x) and Hⁿ = μHE[n]).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (N : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (r : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ V = n → 0 < r → (∀ y ∈ Metric.ball x r, y ∈ N ↔ y - x ∈ V) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (approximate tangent space), applied in step 6 of the parent proof to sets made of open unit faces ("M' has approximate tangent space V_ι at x"), which coincide with the plane of the face near each of their points.

1. The dimension condition dim V = n holds by hypothesis.

2. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Its support is compact, hence bounded: there is R > 0 with f(w) = 0 whenever |w| ≥ R. Let B := ball(0, R) (open, hence Borel).

3. Let 0 < λ < r/R and S_λ := blowUpMap x λ '' N = {λ⁻¹(y − x) : y ∈ N}. Claim: S_λ ∩ B = V ∩ B. If w ∈ S_λ ∩ B, then w = λ⁻¹(y − x) with y ∈ N, and |y − x| = λ|w| < λR < r, so y − x ∈ V by hypothesis and w = λ⁻¹(y − x) ∈ V. Conversely, if w ∈ V ∩ B, let y := x + λw; then |y − x| = λ|w| < r and y − x = λw ∈ V, so y ∈ N by hypothesis, and blowUpMap x λ y = λ⁻¹(λw) = w, so w ∈ S_λ.

4. For every set S ⊆ ℝ^P, since f vanishes off B: ∫_S f dHⁿ = ∫ f d(Hⁿ⌞S) = ∫_B f d(Hⁿ⌞S) (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero) = ∫ f d(Hⁿ⌞(B ∩ S)) (Measure.restrict_restrict, B Borel). Applying this to S = S_λ and S = V and using step 3: ∫_{S_λ} f dHⁿ = ∫_V f dHⁿ for every λ ∈ (0, r/R).

5. The interval (0, r/R) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0, so λ ↦ ∫_{S_λ} f dHⁿ is eventually equal, along 𝓝[>] 0, to the constant ∫_V f dHⁿ, and therefore tends to it (tendsto_const_nhds.congr'). As f was arbitrary, this together with step 1 is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x V. ∎
proof_key_steps: Every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) vanishes outside some ball B(0, R).
For 0 < λ < r/R the blow-up λ⁻¹(N − x) coincides with V inside B(0, R).
So the blow-up integrals equal ∫_V f for all small λ, hence converge to it; with dim V = n this is the approximate tangent space property.

audit.reason: For each compactly supported test function, sufficiently small blow-ups agree with V wherever the function can be nonzero. Restriction to a measurable ball justifies equality of integrals even for arbitrary N, proving the exact tangent predicate.

subproblem.title: A set lying in a translate of a coordinate n-plane V_ι can only have V_ι as approximate tangent space, and unit orientations of it are ±e_ι (Simon Ch. 6, (26)–(27); step 3 of the parent proof)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, ι : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing, A ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P), x ∈ ℝ^P, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P and ξ an n-vector (MultiVector P n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors). Assume (i) a_i = x_i for every a ∈ A and every coordinate i ∉ range ι; (ii) A has approximate tangent space Q at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4: dim Q = n and ∫_{blowUpMap x λ '' A} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), where blowUpMap x λ y = λ⁻¹(y − x) and Hⁿ = μHE[n]); (iii) ξ is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q). Then either ξ(α) = α(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}) for every n-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}) for every n-covector α (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ι : Fin n → Fin P) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ξ : MultiVector P n), StrictMono ι → (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ i, (∀ j, ι j ≠ i) → a i = x i) → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q → IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ α = α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ))) ∨ (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ α = -α (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (ι j) (1 : ℝ)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, (26)–(27), as used in step 3 of the parent proof: on a face of L_n the orientation of Q is ±e_ι because the approximate tangent space there is the face plane V_ι, approximate tangent spaces being determined by their defining limits ("the defining limits determine the measure Hⁿ⌞Q, hence Q"). Here that argument is carried out for an arbitrary set A contained in the translate x + V_ι. Let V := span{e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}}; since ι is injective the e_{ι(j)} are orthonormal, dim V = n, and V = {v ∈ ℝ^P : v_i = 0 for every i ∉ range ι}.

1. Blow-ups lie in V. For λ > 0 and a ∈ A, the vector blowUpMap x λ a = λ⁻¹(a − x) has i-th coordinate λ⁻¹(a_i − x_i) = 0 for every i ∉ range ι, by (i). Hence blowUpMap x λ '' A ⊆ V for every λ > 0.

2. Q ⊆ V. If n = 0, dim Q = 0 forces Q = {0} ⊆ V. Let n ≥ 1 and suppose, for contradiction, q ∈ Q with q ∉ V. V is closed, so ρ := dist(q, V)/2 > 0 and the closed ball B̄(q, ρ) does not meet V. Let f(w) := max(0, ρ − dist(w, q)). f is continuous, nonnegative, vanishes outside the compact ball B̄(q, ρ) (so f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P)), f(q) = ρ > 0, and f = 0 on V. By step 1, f vanishes on blowUpMap x λ '' A, so ∫_{blowUpMap x λ '' A} f dHⁿ = 0 for every λ > 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero); by (ii) these integrals tend to ∫_Q f dHⁿ, hence ∫_Q f dHⁿ = 0. On the other hand, choose an orthonormal basis τ₀ of Q (n vectors) and let ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, ψ(w) := Σ_k w_k τ₀_k, a linear isometry with range Q. By Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and μHE[n] = volume on Euclid n (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), Hⁿ⌞Q = ψ#(volume); ψ is a closed, hence measurable, embedding, so ∫_Q f dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} f(ψ(w)) dw (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map). The function f∘ψ is continuous and nonnegative, has compact support (ψ⁻¹(B̄(q, ρ)) is closed and bounded because ψ is an isometry), and is nonzero at w₀ with ψ(w₀) = q. Lebesgue measure is positive on nonempty open sets and finite on compact sets, so ∫ f∘ψ > 0 (Continuous.integral_pos_of_hasCompactSupport_nonneg_nonzero), a contradiction. Hence Q ⊆ V.

3. Q = V. By (ii), dim Q = n = dim V, and Q ⊆ V; so Q = V (Submodule.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq).

4. The orientation. By (iii) there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with span τ = Q = V and either ξ(α) = α(τ) for all α or ξ(α) = −α(τ) for all α. Each τ_k ∈ V, so τ_k = Σ_j M_{jk} e_{ι(j)} with M_{jk} := ⟨τ_k, e_{ι(j)}⟩. Since τ and (e_{ι(j)})_j are orthonormal bases of V, M is an orthogonal n × n matrix (MᵀM = I), so det M ∈ {1, −1}. For every n-covector α, multilinearity and the alternating property give α(τ) = Σ_{σ ∈ S_n} (∏_k M_{σ(k)k}) α(e_{ι(σ(0))}, …, e_{ι(σ(n−1))}) = Σ_σ sgn(σ) (∏_k M_{σ(k)k}) α(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}) = det(M)·α(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}), the terms with non-injective index maps vanishing. (Equivalently: the restriction of α to V equals α(e_ι)·det_{e_ι} by AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det, and det_{e_ι}(τ) = ±1 for an orthonormal τ by OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real.) Hence ξ(α) = ε·α(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(n−1)}) for all α, where ε := det M or ε := −det M is in {1, −1} and does not depend on α. If ε = 1 the first alternative holds, if ε = −1 the second. ∎
proof_key_steps: Every blow-up λ⁻¹(A − x) lies in V = span{e_{ι(j)}} because A ⊆ x + V.
A C_c test function supported near q ∈ Q ∖ V has zero blow-up integrals but positive integral over Q (Hⁿ⌞Q is Lebesgue measure transported by a linear isometry), so Q ⊆ V.
Equal dimensions give Q = V.
An orthonormal frame τ of V equals e_ι·M with M orthogonal, so α(τ) = det(M)·α(e_ι) with det M = ±1, and ξ = ±e_ι.

audit.reason: The separating compactly supported function forces the tangent plane into the coordinate plane; equal dimensions give equality. The orthonormal change-of-basis determinant supplies a single sign valid for every covector, including degree zero. No measurability hypothesis on A is needed.

1. Coordinate covectors. 2. The data. For l < n let J_l := ι ∘ Fin.succAbove l : Fin m → Fin P. It is strictly increasing (a composition of strictly increasing maps) with range J_l = range ι ∖ {ι(l)} (ι injective), so l ↦ J_l is injective. Let π : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ, π(x)_k := x_{ι(k)} − z_{ι(k)} (affine, C^∞), and ν(x) := Σ_{i ∉ range ι} (x_i − z_i)² (a polynomial, ≥ 0). Let η : ℝ → [0, 1] be C^∞ with η(t) = 1 for t ≤ δ²/4 and η(t) = 0 for t ≥ δ², e.g. η(t) := Real.smoothTransition((δ² − t)/(3δ²/4)) (smoothTransition is C^∞, [0, 1]-valued, 0 on (−∞, 0] and 1 on [1, ∞)). Put χ := η∘ν and ω(x) := Σ_{l<n} ((−1)^l χ(x) g_l(π(x))) • dx^{J_l}.

3. ω is a test form. ω is a finite sum of C^∞ real functions (products of χ and g_l∘π; g is C^∞ and π is affine) times constant covectors, hence C^∞ (ContDiff.smul with a constant, ContDiff.sum). If ω(x) ≠ 0 then χ(x) ≠ 0, so ν(x) < δ², and g(π(x)) ≠ 0. Hence tsupport ω ⊆ Z := {x : ν(x) ≤ δ²} ∩ π⁻¹(tsupport g), which is closed; Z is bounded, since for x ∈ Z the coordinates x_{ι(k)} = z_{ι(k)} + π(x)_k range over a bounded set (tsupport g is compact) and |x_i − z_i| ≤ δ for i ∉ range ι. So ω has compact support and ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) = TestFormOn univ m (tsupport ω ⊆ univ trivially).

4. (i). Fix x. By CC-ii with N := n, the injective family (J_l)_{l<n} and c_l := (−1)^l χ(x) g_l(π(x)): covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) = (Σ_l χ(x)² g_l(π(x))²)^{1/2} = χ(x)·|g(π(x))| (on Euclid n, |w|² = Σ_l w_l², EuclideanSpace.norm_eq; χ ≥ 0) ≤ 1, because 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1 and |g| ≤ 1.

5. (ii). Let x ∈ tsupport ω ⊆ Z and y := π(x) ∈ tsupport g. Since ι is injective, Φ_p(y) has coordinate z_{ι(k)} + y_k = x_{ι(k)} at ι(k) and z_i at i ∉ range ι, so |x − Φ_p(y)|² = Σ_{i∉range ι} (x_i − z_i)² = ν(x) ≤ δ², i.e. dist(x, Φ_p(y)) ≤ δ.

6. (iii). Fix y ∈ ℝⁿ and x₀ := Φ_p(y); then π(x₀) = y and ν(x₀) = 0 < δ²/4. By continuity of ν, χ = 1 on an open neighbourhood O of x₀, so ω(x) = Σ_l (−1)^l g_l(π(x)) • dx^{J_l} for x ∈ O. ω is C^∞, hence differentiable at x₀, so by the exterior-derivative formula (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative = Mathlib extDeriv; exteriorDerivative_apply / extDeriv_apply) dω(x₀)(v) = Σ_{i<n} (−1)^i · D[x ↦ ω(x)(Fin.removeNth i v)](x₀)(v_i). For v = e_ι, Fin.removeNth i e_ι = (e_{ι(succAbove i c)})_{c<m} = e_{J_i} (this holds after unfolding, not syntactically: use `show` or `simp only [Fin.removeNth, Function.comp_apply]` to put it in the form fun c => EuclideanSpace.single (J_i c) 1 of CC-i before rewriting). By CC-i (J_l = J_i iff l = i), ω(x)(e_{J_i}) = Σ_l (−1)^l χ(x) g_l(π(x)) dx^{J_l}(e_{J_i}) = (−1)^i χ(x) g_i(π(x)) for every x, and = (−1)^i g_i(π(x)) for x ∈ O. A derivative at x₀ depends only on values near x₀ (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), and π(x₀ + t e_{ι(i)}) = y + t ê_i (ι injective), so D[x ↦ ω(x)(e_{J_i})](x₀)(e_{ι(i)}) = (−1)^i (Dg(y) ê_i)_i. Therefore dω(Φ_p(y))(e_p) = Σ_i (−1)^i (−1)^i (Dg(y) ê_i)_i = Σ_i ⟨Dg(y) ê_i, ê_i⟩ = trace(Dg(y)), the trace of a linear map being the sum of the diagonal entries of its matrix in the basis (ê_i) (LinearMap.trace_eq_matrix_trace with EuclideanSpace.basisFun and LinearMap.toMatrix_apply). ∎

Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, displays (26)–(28) and (33), in the form of steps 2–3 of the parent proof: because Q is integer multiplicity, the face densities are read off from an IMRep of Q (using (IMC)(a)) instead of the constancy-theorem argument. Dependencies: FG = sibling dor_lmb_fcd_fr_face_geometry; PO = sibling dor_lmb_fcd_fr_plane_orientation; CC = sibling dor_lmb_fcd_fr_coordinate_covectors; C1 = reused sibling dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support; IMC = reused sibling cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (part (a)). For p = (z, ι) ∈ s: A_p := Φ_p(Q₁), F_p the closed face, e_p = (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}).

1. Faces (FG). For p ∈ s: Φ_p(y) ∈ F_p for y in the closed cube, in particular A_p ⊆ F_p (FG(5)); F_p is closed (FG(8)) and bounded (FG(7)), hence compact; Φ_p is an isometry (FG(6)), hence a closed and measurable embedding, so A_p is Borel; for q ∈ s, q ≠ p, A_p ∩ F_q = ∅ (FG(9)), so the A_p (p ∈ s) are pairwise disjoint. By FG(3), Hⁿ⌞F_p = Φ_p#(volume⌞Q₁); hence for every Borel h : ℝ^P → ℝ, h∘Φ_p is integrable on Q₁ iff h is integrable for Hⁿ⌞F_p (MeasurableEmbedding.integrable_map_iff), and ∫_{F_p} h dHⁿ = ∫_{Q₁} h(Φ_p(y)) dy (FG(4)).

2. An IMRep and its measure. Since Q is integer multiplicity, there is an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) in univ representing Q: M is Borel, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is Borel with θ ≥ 1 on M and ∫⁻_{M∩K'} θ dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K', ξ is AE-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, and Q(ω) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every test form ω. Let μ := R.measure = θ·Hⁿ⌞M, so μ(B) = ∫⁻_{M∩B} θ dHⁿ for Borel B. By C1 (U = univ is open), M_W(Q) = μ(W) for every open W; in particular M(Q) = M_{ℝ^P}(Q) = μ(ℝ^P). For compact K', Hⁿ(M ∩ K') ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K'} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (θ ≥ 1 on M).

3. M is carried by the open faces. W₀ := ℝ^P ∖ E is open (E closed). If ω is admissible for M_{W₀}(Q), then tsupport ω ⊆ W₀ is disjoint from E, so Q(ω) = 0 by hypothesis; hence M_{W₀}(Q) = 0, so μ(W₀) = ∫⁻_{M∖E} θ dHⁿ = 0, and as θ ≥ 1 on M, Hⁿ(M ∖ E) = 0. By hypothesis and Borel measurability of E, Hⁿ(E ∖ ⋃_{p∈s} A_p) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply'). Let M_p := M ∩ A_p (Borel, pairwise disjoint). Then Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_{p∈s} M_p) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∖ E) + Hⁿ(E ∖ ⋃_p A_p) = 0.

4. Orientation on each face. Fix p = (z, ι) ∈ s. (a) By the IMRep field orients, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, and hence for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_p ⊆ M, there is a linear subspace Q_x such that M has approximate tangent space Q_x at x and ξ(x) is a unit orientation of Q_x. (b) By IMC(a), applied with U := univ and the Borel sets M_p ⊆ M (finiteness hypothesis from step 2), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_p and every subspace Q', M_p has approximate tangent space Q' at x iff M does. (c) Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_p, M_p has approximate tangent space Q_x at x and ξ(x) is a unit orientation of Q_x. Every a ∈ M_p ⊆ A_p ⊆ F_p satisfies a_i = z_i for i ∉ range ι, and so does x ∈ M_p; thus a_i = x_i for all a ∈ M_p and i ∉ range ι. By PO (with A := M_p), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_p there is ε(x) ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(x)(α) = ε(x) α(e_p) for every n-covector α.

5. A Borel sign. By CC with k := n there is an n-covector α_p := dx^ι with α_p(e_p) = 1 (CC (i) with I = J = ι, ι strictly increasing). The function x ↦ ξ(x)(α_p) is AE-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M (ξ is, and evaluation at the fixed covector α_p is a continuous linear map on MultiVector P n), so it agrees Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. with a Borel function h_p (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk, or AEMeasurable.mk). Let σ_p(x) := 1 if h_p(x) ≥ 0 and σ_p(x) := −1 otherwise (Borel). Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. statements hold Hⁿ⌞M_p-a.e. (M_p ⊆ M), so for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M_p step 4 gives ξ(x)(α_p) = ε(x)·α_p(e_p) = ε(x) ∈ {1, −1} and h_p(x) = ξ(x)(α_p); hence σ_p(x) = ε(x) and ξ(x)(α) = σ_p(x)·α(e_p) for every α.

6. The densities. For p ∈ s define f_p(x) := θ(x) σ_p(x) 1_{M_p}(x) on ℝ^P and u_p(y) := θ(Φ_p(y)) σ_p(Φ_p(y)) 1_M(Φ_p(y)) on ℝⁿ; for p ∉ s put u_p := 0. subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1 (the faces F ∈ 𝓛_n of the grid, and displays (26)–(33), where Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0 is used when Q is decomposed over the open faces), as used in steps 1(b), 1(c) and 2 of the parent proof (every point of L_n ∖ L_{n−1} lies in exactly one open face, only finitely many faces meet the compact K, diam F_p ≤ √P, Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0). Dependency: FG = sibling dor_lmb_fcd_fr_face_geometry. n := m + 1, and L' := {x : there is a finset t with P ≤ m + |t| and x_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ t} (the (n−1)-skeleton L_{n−1}: points with at least P − m integer coordinates).

0. Hⁿ(L') = 0, i.e. μHE[m+1](L') = 0. (This is the argument of the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmcdtfr_skeleton_null, whose frozen type is exactly this equation; its Lean proof is in candidate commit 09516d6d883db6c4d6e24410e2a32da5a8ae36f4 and may be copied, but only as a local `have` inside this theorem's proof: do not add a top-level declaration named cmcdtfr_skeleton_null or any other cmcdtfr_* name, which belong to another DAG branch.) μH[d] is Mathlib's unnormalized d-dimensional Hausdorff measure and μHE[d] = c_d • μH[d] for a constant c_d (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def), so it suffices to show μH[m+1](L') = 0.
 (a) Countable cover. For a finset t and z : Fin P → ℤ let A(t, z) := {x : x_i = z_i for i ∈ t}. If x ∈ L' with witness t, choose z with x_i = z_i for i ∈ t; then x ∈ A(t, z). So L' ⊆ ⋃_{t : P ≤ m + |t|} ⋃_{z : Fin P → ℤ} A(t, z), a countable union (finitely many t; Fin P → ℤ is countable), and by countable subadditivity (measure_iUnion_null, measure_mono_null) it suffices that μH[m+1](A(t, z)) = 0 for each t with P ≤ m + |t| and each z.
 (b) Parametrization. Fix such t, z. S := {i : Fin P // i ∉ t} has r := P − |t| ≤ m elements (Fintype.card_subtype_compl). Let g : (S → ℝ) → ℝ^P, g(w) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => if h : i ∈ t then (z i : ℝ) else w ⟨i, h⟩). For the sup metrics, w ↦ (i ↦ g(w)_i) is 1-Lipschitz into Fin P → ℝ (each coordinate is constant or a coordinate of w: dist_le_pi_dist, dist_pi_le_iff), and WithLp.toLp 2 is Lipschitz (PiLp.lipschitzWith_toLp); so g is K-Lipschitz for some K. A(t, z) ⊆ g(univ): for x ∈ A(t, z) take w_⟨j,h⟩ := x_j.
 (c) On S → ℝ, μH[card S] = volume (hausdorffMeasure_pi_real), so every ball B(0, k) has finite μH[r]-measure (measure_ball_lt_top). As r < m + 1, Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top (d₁ = r < d₂ = m + 1) gives μH[m+1](B(0, k)) = 0; univ = ⋃_{k∈ℕ} B(0, k) (Metric.iUnion_ball_nat), so μH[m+1](univ : Set (S → ℝ)) = 0.
 (d) μH[m+1](g(univ)) ≤ K^{m+1}·μH[m+1](univ) = 0 (LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le), hence μH[m+1](A(t, z)) = 0. By (a), μH[m+1](L') = 0, and μHE[m+1](L') = c_{m+1} • 0 = 0 (Measure.smul_apply). This covers P ≤ m (t = ∅ is a witness and L' = ℝ^P) and P = 0.

1. L_n is closed. L_n = ⋃_{t : P ≤ n + |t|} ⋂_{i∈t} {x : x_i ∈ ℤ}. Each {x : x_i ∈ ℤ} is the preimage of the closed set ℤ ⊆ ℝ (the range of Int.cast, closed because distinct integers are at distance ≥ 1) under the continuous coordinate map x ↦ x_i. Finite intersections, and the finite union over the finitely many finsets t ⊆ Fin P, of closed sets are closed.

2. The finite family. Let 𝒫 := {p = (z, ι) : ι strictly increasing and F_p ∩ K ≠ ∅}. K is bounded, so there is R ≥ 0 with |x_i| ≤ R for all x ∈ K and all i. If x ∈ F_p ∩ K, then z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 for i ∈ range ι, giving |z_i| ≤ R + 1, and z_i = x_i for i ∉ range ι, giving |z_i| ≤ R. Hence 𝒫 ⊆ {z ∈ ℤ^P : |z_i| ≤ R + 1 for all i} × (Fin n → Fin P), a product of two finite sets; so 𝒫 is finite. Let s be the finset with elements 𝒫. Every p ∈ s has ι strictly increasing.

3. Thickening. Let p ∈ s and choose k ∈ F_p ∩ K. For x ∈ F_p, FG(7) gives dist(x, k) ≤ √P, so x ∈ cthickening(√P, K) (Metric.mem_cthickening_of_dist_le). Hence F_p ⊆ cthickening(√P, K).

4. Points of (L_n ∩ K) ∖ L' lie in open faces of s. Let x ∈ L_n ∩ K with x ∉ L'. Let S := {i : x_i ∉ ℤ} and T := {i : x_i ∈ ℤ}, the complement of S. Since x ∈ L_n there is t with P ≤ n + |t| and x_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ t, i.e. t ⊆ T; so |T| ≥ P − n. Since x ∉ L', the finset T (all of whose coordinates are integers) does not satisfy P ≤ m + |T|, so |T| ≤ P − m − 1 = P − n. Hence |T| = P − n and |S| = n. Let ι : Fin n → Fin P be the strictly increasing enumeration of S (Finset.orderEmbOfFin), so range ι = S. Put z_i := ⌊x_i⌋ for all i and y_k := x_{ι(k)} − ⌊x_{ι(k)}⌋ (fractional part) for k < n; since x_{ι(k)} ∉ ℤ, 0 < y_k < 1, so y ∈ Q₁. For p := (z, ι), Φ_p(y) = x: since ι is injective, the coordinate of Φ_p(y) at ι(k) is z_{ι(k)} + y_k = x_{ι(k)}, and at i ∉ S it is z_i = ⌊x_i⌋ = x_i because x_i ∈ ℤ. By FG(5), x = Φ_p(y) ∈ F_p, and x ∈ K; so F_p ∩ K ≠ ∅ and p ∈ s.

5. The almost-everywhere statement. By step 4, the set B of x ∈ L_n ∩ K for which there are no p ∈ s and y ∈ Q₁ with Φ_p(y) = x is contained in L'. L_n ∩ K is closed (step 1; K is compact, hence closed), hence Borel, so (μHE[n]⌞(L_n ∩ K))({x : no such p, y}) = μHE[n]({x : no such p, y} ∩ L_n ∩ K) = μHE[n](B) ≤ μHE[n](L') = 0 (step 0; Measure.restrict_apply' with the Borel set L_n ∩ K). This is the claimed statement for μHE[n]⌞(L_n ∩ K)-almost every x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0: cover L_{n−1} by the countably many coordinate planes A(t, z), each in the image of a Lipschitz map from a space of dimension P − |t| ≤ m < m + 1, and use μHE = c·μH.
L_n is a finite union of finite intersections of closed coordinate conditions x_i ∈ ℤ.
Faces meeting the bounded set K have bounded integer corners, so they form a finite set s.
diam F_p ≤ √P (face_geometry) gives F_p ⊆ cthickening(√P, K) for p ∈ s.
A point of (L_n ∩ K) ∖ L_{n−1} has exactly n non-integer coordinates and equals Φ_p(fractional parts) for p = (⌊x⌋, increasing enumeration of those coordinates) ∈ s.
Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0 (step 0) gives the covering for μHE[n]⌞(L_n ∩ K)-a.e. x.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, (28) (second part, "by the obvious modifications of the arguments in the proof of the Constancy Theorem (2.34) and in 2.35"), in the form of step 4 of the parent proof, with the disjoint open neighbourhoods V_p of the open faces taken relative to the finitely many faces of s (here called W_p). Dependencies: FG = sibling dor_lmb_fcd_fr_face_geometry; DF = sibling dor_lmb_fcd_fr_divergence_form. For p ∈ s let A_p := Φ_p(Q₁) (nonempty: Φ_p(½, …, ½) ∈ A_p) and F_p the closed face; recall A_p ⊆ F_p (FG(5)).

1. Disjoint open neighbourhoods. For p ∈ s let W_p := {x ∈ ℝ^P : infDist(x, A_p) < infDist(x, A_q) for every q ∈ s with q ≠ p} (W_p = ℝ^P if s = {p}). As x ↦ infDist(x, A) is continuous (1-Lipschitz), W_p is a finite intersection of open sets, hence open. The W_p are pairwise disjoint: x ∈ W_p ∩ W_q with p ≠ q would give infDist(x, A_p) < infDist(x, A_q) < infDist(x, A_p).

2. Σ_{p∈s} M_{W_p}(∂Q) ≤ M(∂Q). Write T := ∂Q ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) and, for every pair p, 𝒜_p := massAdmissibleOn univ m W_p (test m-forms ω with tsupport ω ⊆ W_p and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x); 0 ∈ 𝒜_p, and M_{W_p}(T) = sSup ((ω ↦ ofReal(T(ω))) '' 𝒜_p) = ⨆_{ω ∈ 𝒜_p} ofReal(T(ω)) (sSup_image'). (a) Family bound. Let (ω_p)_{p∈s} be any family with ω_p ∈ 𝒜_p. Put ω'_p := ω_p if T(ω_p) ≥ 0 and ω'_p := 0 otherwise; then ofReal(T(ω_p)) = ofReal(T(ω'_p)) and T(ω'_p) ≥ 0. Let ω := Σ_{p∈s} ω'_p, a test m-form. For each x at most one ω'_p(x) is nonzero (ω'_p(x) ≠ 0 gives x ∈ tsupport ω'_p ⊆ W_p, and the W_p, p ∈ s, are pairwise disjoint by step 1), so covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) is 0 or covectorEuclideanNorm(ω'_p(x)) ≤ 1; thus ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ m univ and, by linearity of T and ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg, Σ_{p∈s} ofReal(T(ω_p)) = ofReal(Σ_{p∈s} T(ω'_p)) = ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ T.massOn univ = M(T) (le_massOn). (b) Suprema. Index families by i : (p : pairs) → 𝒜_p (all pairs p, so that the index type does not depend on s) and put f_p(i) := ofReal(T(i p)); then ⨆_i f_p(i) = ⨆_{ω∈𝒜_p} ofReal(T(ω)) = M_{W_p}(T) (every ω ∈ 𝒜_p is i p for some family i, the 𝒜_q being nonempty). The family index is directed for all f_p simultaneously: for two families i, j choose at each p the member of {i p, j p} with the larger value of f_p. So ENNReal.finsetSum_iSup gives Σ_{p∈s} M_{W_p}(T) = Σ_{p∈s} ⨆_i f_p(i) = ⨆_i Σ_{p∈s} f_p(i) ≤ M(T) by (a). Hence Σ_{p∈s} M_{W_p}(∂Q) ≤ M(∂Q).

3. The numbers V_p. Since M(∂Q) ≠ ∞, step 2 gives M_{W_p}(∂Q) < ∞ for every p ∈ s. Put V_p := M_{W_p}(∂Q).toReal ≥ 0 for p ∈ s (and V_p := 0 otherwise). Then ENNReal.ofReal(Σ_{p∈s} V_p) = Σ_{p∈s} ofReal(V_p) = Σ_{p∈s} M_{W_p}(∂Q) ≤ M(∂Q).

4. A separation constant. Fix p ∈ s and g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, C^∞, with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g| ≤ 1. G := Φ_p(tsupport g) is compact (Φ_p is continuous by FG(6)) and G ⊆ A_p. For q ∈ s with q ≠ p, FG(9) gives G ∩ F_q = ∅; F_q is closed (FG(8)) and nonempty, so w ↦ infDist(w, F_q) is continuous and positive on G (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos) and, if G ≠ ∅, attains a positive minimum on G (IsCompact.exists_isMinOn). Choose δ > 0 with 3δ ≤ infDist(w, F_q) for every w ∈ G and every q ∈ s ∖ {p} (δ := 1 if G = ∅ or s = {p}).

5. The test form. DF applied to p, g and δ gives a test (n−1)-form ω with covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x, such that every x ∈ tsupport ω satisfies dist(x, Φ_p(y)) ≤ δ for some y ∈ tsupport g, and dω(Φ_p(y))(e_p) = trace(Dg(y)) for every y ∈ ℝⁿ.

6. tsupport ω ⊆ W_p. Let x ∈ tsupport ω and y ∈ tsupport g with dist(x, Φ_p(y)) ≤ δ; w := Φ_p(y) ∈ G ⊆ A_p, so infDist(x, A_p) ≤ δ. For q ∈ s ∖ {p} and a ∈ A_q ⊆ F_q: dist(x, a) ≥ dist(w, a) − dist(x, w) ≥ 3δ − δ = 2δ, so infDist(x, A_q) ≥ 2δ > δ ≥ infDist(x, A_p). Hence x ∈ W_p. With step 5, ω is admissible for M_{W_p}(∂Q).

7. Evaluation. ∂Q(ω) = Q(dω), and the hypothesis applied to the test n-form dω gives ∂Q(ω) = Σ_{q∈s} ∫_{Q₁} u_q(y) dω(Φ_q(y))(e_q) dy. Let q ∈ s, q ≠ p, and y ∈ Q₁; then Φ_q(y) ∈ A_q, and Φ_q(y) ∉ tsupport ω, for otherwise Φ_q(y) ∈ W_p (step 6) would give infDist(Φ_q(y), A_p) < infDist(Φ_q(y), A_q) = 0, impossible.
